narr: The atmosphere on September 7th remained well saturated, with PWAT values into the 1.9 to 2.2 inch range. This deep moisture combined with the passage of a frontal boundary that extended along the coast and continued to move offshore during the early morning hours produced periods of heavy rainfall across South Texas. This was particularly true along the Rio Grande. As the day progressed, moisture convergence, daytime heating, and subtle impulses of energy embedded in the northwest flow aloft were enough to support training thunderstorms across the Victoria Crossroads, leading to isolated flash flooding.

Flash flooding forced the closure of the Navarro Street underpass on Sunday, blocking traffic at the entrances on East North Street, Navarro Street and Goodwin Avenue. City officials said barricades were placed at all entry points to keep drivers out of high water. Crews are monitoring the area and will reopen the intersection once conditions improve. Police say the intersection could remain closed until Monday.
